units: basis points of notional, charged on EACH side of a round trip (entry and exit)
principle: Conservative by construction: every component is set at or above what a small account would pay at the touch on a normal day. A rule that only works under a cheaper model does not count as working.

us_equity_etf_large.basis: SPY trades at a 1-cent spread on a ~$700 price (~0.14 bp, half ~0.07 bp); 0.5 bp is ~7x that. Commission 0.5 bp stands in for zero-commission broker fees plus SEC/FINRA TAF sell-side fees. Slippage 2 bp covers market-on-trigger fills off 5-minute bar closes and level touches, which a resting order would not get at the printed level.

us_equity_large_cap.basis: Typical large-cap quoted spreads are 1-5 bp; half-spread taken at the top of that range. Slippage 5 bp for close-to-close execution through MOC/near-close orders.

examples: Russell 2000 / sub-$2B names, including most VS1 sector-panel issuers
us_equity_small_cap.basis: Small caps routinely quote 10-50 bp spreads; 15 bp half-spread plus 15 bp impact is a deliberate penalty so thin-name edges must clear ~60 bp round trip.

examples: ETH spot on a retail venue
crypto_major_spot.basis: Retail crypto venues charge 10-60 bp taker fees or an equivalent embedded spread markup; 25 bp commission plus a 10 bp half-spread is the conservative middle of that band for an account of GRID's size.
